    Found by elaborating an application rather than trusting the component form:
    destructuring the Prop-valued IsGaloisQuotient directly into the Type-valued
    RepresentableBy conclusion FAILS -- 'Exists.casesOn can only eliminate into
    Prop'. So the four-component theorem was not usable by any G2 consumer as it
    stood. Fixed here rather than left for the next lane to hit.
    
     * nonempty_representableBy_picEt_of_isGaloisQuotient -- the Nonempty form, which
       is where Classical.choice is spent (the I-1405 repair, same trap).
     * seamClauseOne_of_isGaloisQuotient -- clause (1) in full; needs NO choice in
       that step, because clause (1) is itself an existential.
     * seamClauseOne_of_isGaloisQuotient_canonical -- rho eliminated too, by stating
       the quotient at semilinearGalActionOfRepresentableBy. Minimal-input form.
    
    Also confirms the hcov spelling matches representableBy_of_galInvariantEquiv's on
    the nose (Scheme.etaleTopologyOver), so pic-a's row plugs in directly.
    
    lake build EXIT=0 (8695 jobs); all four axiom-clean vs fgaPicardRepresentability
    firing sorryAx in the same probe. Closes no sorry.

Author:     Archon Horizon <archon@archon-horizon.local>

    G1's invariance match is FREE at the canonical Galois action
    
    isInvariantMatch_canonical: the IsInvariantMatch hypothesis that
    Picard/PicEtDescentGoal.lean carries as campaign G1's undischarged debt holds at
    semilinearGalActionOfRepresentableBy C rep, for every test, with NO hypothesis
    beyond rep and the curve's own binders -- arbitrary field k, arbitrary extension
    k'/k, no finiteness, no separability, no IsGalois, no condition on Gal(k'/k).
    
    So G1 is not an input of the etale-descent route: the descent goal's four inputs
    are three (rep, the Galois quotient, hcov).
    
    Free rather than fortunate, because the canonical action's gamma-component IS
    twistMor gamma, which is DEFINED by transporting the functor action
    galoisActionPicEt along rep. Three steps, each formal:
     * isEquivariant_iff_galTwistMor -- equivariance of the underlying scheme map is
       the same square read in the k'-slice; galTwistMor is that packaging of
       pullbackGalMap, and twistTest_eq_restrictTest_galTwistMor is the slice form of
       the rfl-identity I-1455 already records.
     * homEquiv_twist_comp -- THE STEP: rep.homEquiv of the square's right side is
       (galoisActionPicEt gamma).inv at rep.homEquiv phi, by naturality at phi.op.
       twistMor was built from that natural transformation, so naturality un-builds it.
     * crossBaseIso_galoisActionPicEt_inv -- transport along picEt_crossBaseIso leaves
       picEt C applied to restrictTest_twistTestFunctor_iso, whose components are the
       identity on underlying schemes.
    Composed: equivariance at gamma IS invariance at gamma^-1, and since both
    predicates quantify over the whole group and gamma -> gamma^-1 is a bijection of
    it, they coincide. That Gal(k'/k) is a group is all that is used about it.
    
    This SUBSUMES isInvariantMatch_of_subsingleton, the trivial-Galois-group
    measurement: it was the degenerate case of a fact holding at every extension.
    
    Closes no sorry: rep is still the campaign's undischarged output and clause (1)
    field 1 is witnessed for no curve. hcov's non-vacuity is untouched.
    
    lake env lean EXIT=0, zero errors, zero warnings, zero sorries.

    Root the invariance match, add its payoff forms, correct the prose it falsified
    
     * PicEtInvariantMatch.lean: §4 adds the two forms a consumer should now call --
       representableBy_picEt_of_galoisQuotient_canonical and
       seamClauseOne_of_isGaloisQuotient_noMatch. Both drop the hmatch argument AND the
       externally-supplied action: their inputs are rep, a Galois quotient of the action
       rep itself determines, hcov, and (for clause (1)) local finiteness of the quotient.
       So the etale-descent route between rep and clause (1) field 1 now has TWO named
       antecedents -- pic-f's non-affine Galois quotient and pic-a's hcov.
       Also: eight maxHeartbeats sites now carry the explanation the style linter asks
       for. Those warnings do NOT appear under `lake env lean`, only under `lake build`,
       which is why the earlier per-file check reported clean.
     * AlgebraicJacobian.lean: root the module.
     * PicEtDescentGoal.lean: my own r1 docstring said IsInvariantMatch is "not proved
       here", called it "satisfiable but not measured non-vacuous", and said exhibiting a
       model at a nontrivial automorphism was open and "is what would make G1's cost a
       real number". My commit made all of that false. Corrected in place rather than
       left to read as audited self-criticism, and the withdrawal is scoped: the SAME
       paragraph's claim about hcov is UNCHANGED and still stands, so
       representableBy_picEt_of_degenerate remains the honest caution for the k'=k site.
       isInvariantMatch_of_subsingleton is now subsumed, not cautionary.
    
    VERIFIED: lake build AlgebraicJacobian.Picard.PicEtInvariantMatch, 8696 jobs, EXIT=0,
    zero warnings from the file, zero sorries. Full signatures printed (per I-1292, not
    read off headers): isInvariantMatch_canonical carries NO Algebra.IsSeparable, NO
    Module.Finite, no IsGalois -- only Field k, Field k', Algebra k k' and the curve's two
    binders; seamClauseOne_of_isGaloisQuotient_noMatch takes rep, hq, hcov, hlft and no
    hmatch. All axiom-clean [propext, Classical.choice, Quot.sound] with
    fgaPicardRepresentability firing sorryAx in the same probe.

   191	Defining `Jacobian C := 𝟙_ (Over (Spec (.of k)))` *unconditionally* (the terminal object,
   192	i.e. `Spec k`) compiles and discharges three of the four instances for free, but the
   193	fourth instance `SmoothOfRelativeDimension (genus C) (𝟙_ _).hom` would force `genus C = 0`,
   194	which is mathematically wrong for any curve of genus `≥ 1`. The terminal-object definition
   195	is therefore forbidden when `genus C > 0`. The witness-based definition avoids this
   196	issue: the witness's `J` is `Pic⁰_{C/k}`, which is `Spec k` exactly when `genus C = 0`
   197	and the honest Albanese object otherwise.
   198	-/
   199	
   200	set_option autoImplicit false
   201	
   202	universe u
   203	
   204	open CategoryTheory Limits MonoidalCategory CartesianMonoidalCategory MonObj
   205	
   206	namespace AlgebraicGeometry
   207	
   208	variable {k : Type u} [Field k] (C : Over (Spec (.of k)))
   209	  [SmoothOfRelativeDimension 1 C.hom]
   210	  [IsProper C.hom]
   211	  [GeometricallyIrreducible C.hom]
   212	
   213	/-- The Albanese universal property for a pointed smooth proper curve `(C, P)`.
   214	An object `J` (with abelian-variety structure) is the Albanese of `(C, P)` if it
   215	receives a universal pointed morphism `C ⟶ J` sending `P` to the identity. -/
   216	def IsAlbanese (C : Over (Spec (.of k))) (P : 𝟙_ (Over (Spec (.of k))) ⟶ C)
   217	    (J : Over (Spec (.of k)))
   218	    [GrpObj J] [IsProper J.hom] [Smooth J.hom] [GeometricallyIrreducible J.hom] : Prop :=
   219	  ∃ α : C ⟶ J, P ≫ α = η[J] ∧
   220	    ∀ {A : Over (Spec (.of k))} [GrpObj A] [IsProper A.hom]
   221	      [Smooth A.hom] [GeometricallyIrreducible A.hom] (f : C ⟶ A) (_ : P ≫ f = η[A]),
   222	      ∃! (g : J ⟶ A), f = α ≫ g
   223	
   224	namespace IsAlbanese
   225	
   226	noncomputable def ofCurve {k : Type u} [Field k] {C : Over (Spec (.of k))}
   227	    {P : 𝟙_ _ ⟶ C} {J : Over (Spec (.of k))} [GrpObj J] [IsProper J.hom] [Smooth J.hom]
   228	    [GeometricallyIrreducible J.hom] (h : IsAlbanese C P J) : C ⟶ J :=
   229	  Classical.choose h
   230	
   231	lemma comp_ofCurve {k : Type u} [Field k] {C : Over (Spec (.of k))}
   232	    {P : 𝟙_ _ ⟶ C} {J : Over (Spec (.of k))} [GrpObj J] [IsProper J.hom] [Smooth J.hom]
   233	    [GeometricallyIrreducible J.hom] (h : IsAlbanese C P J) :
   234	    P ≫ h.ofCurve = η[J] :=
   235	  (Classical.choose_spec h).1

     7	% [running head: CHAPTER III. JACOBIAN VARIETIES, page 104]
     8	
     9	\DeclareMathOperator{\Hom}{Hom}
    10	\DeclareMathOperator{\Gal}{Gal}
    11	
    12	\section*{6 \quad The Jacobian variety as Albanese variety; autoduality}
    13	
    14	Throughout this section $C$ will be a complete nonsingular curve of genus
    15	$g > 0$ over a field $k$, and $J$ will be its Jacobian variety.
    16	
    17	\paragraph{Proposition 6.1.}
    18	\textit{Let $P$ be a $k$-rational point on $C$. The map
    19	$f^P \colon C \to J$ has the following universal property: for any map
    20	$\varphi \colon C \to A$ from $C$ into an abelian variety sending $P$ to $0$,
    21	there is a unique homomorphism $\psi \colon J \to A$ such that
    22	$\varphi = \psi \circ f^P$.}
    23	
    24	\paragraph{Proof.}
    25	Consider the map
    26	\[
    27	  (P_1, \dots, P_g) \mapsto \sum_i \psi(P_i) \colon C^g \to A.
    28	  % [sic: printed "\psi(P_i)"; presumably "\varphi(P_i)" is intended, since \psi is being constructed]
    29	\]
    30	Clearly this is symmetric, and so it factors through $C^{(g)}$. It therefore
    31	defines a rational map $\psi \colon J \to A$, which (I 3.2) shows to be a
    32	regular map. It is clear from the construction that $\psi \circ f^P = \varphi$
    33	(note that $f^P$ is the composite of
    34	$Q \mapsto Q + (g-1)P \colon C \to C^{(g)}$ with
    35	$f^{(g)} \colon C^{(g)} \to J$). In particular, $\psi$ maps $0$ to $0$, and
    36	(I 1.2) shows that it is therefore a homomorphism. If $\psi'$ is a second
    37	homomorphism such that $\psi' \circ f^P = \varphi$, then $\psi$ and $\psi'$
    38	agree on $f^P(C) + \dots + f^P(C)$ ($g$ copies), which is the whole of $J$.
    39	\hfill $\square$
    40	
    41	\paragraph{Corollary 6.2.}
    42	\textit{Let $\mathcal{N}$ be a divisorial correspondence between $(C, P)$ and
    43	$J$ such that $(1 \times f^P)^* \mathcal{N} \approx \mathcal{L}^P$; then
    44	$\mathcal{N} \approx \mathcal{M}^P$ (notations as in \S 2 and (1.7)).}
    45	
    46	\paragraph{Proof.}
    47	Because of (I 5.13), we can assume $k$ to be algebraically closed. According
    48	to (1.7) there is a unique map $\varphi \colon J \to J$ such that
    49	$\mathcal{N} \approx (1 \times \varphi)^* \mathcal{M}^P$. On points $\varphi$
    50	is the map sending $a \in J(k)$ to the unique $b$ such that
    51	$\mathcal{M}^P | C \times \{b\} \approx \mathcal{N} | C \times \{a\}$. By
    52	assumption,
    53	\[
    54	  \mathcal{N} | C \times \{f^P Q\}
    55	  \approx \mathcal{L}^P | C \times \{Q\}
    56	  \approx \mathcal{M}^P | C \times \{f^P Q\},
    57	\]
    58	and so $(\varphi \circ f^P)(Q) = f^P(Q)$ for all $Q$. Now (6.1) shows that
    59	$f$ is the identity map. % [sic: printed "$f$"; presumably "\varphi" is intended]
    60	\hfill $\square$
    61	
    62	\paragraph{Corollary 6.3.}
    63	\textit{Let $C_1$ and $C_2$ be curves over $k$ with $k$-rational points $P_1$
    64	and $P_2$, and let $J_1$ and $J_2$ be their Jacobians. There is a one-to-one
    65	correspondence between $\Hom_k(J_1, J_2)$ and the set of isomorphism classes
    66	of divisorial correspondences between $(C_1, P_1)$ and $(C_2, P_2)$.}
    67	
    68	\paragraph{Proof.}
    69	A divisorial correspondence between $(C_2, P_2)$ and $(C_1, P_1)$ gives rise
    70	to a morphism $(C_1, P_1) \to J_2$ (by 1.7), and this morphism gives rise to
    71	homomorphism $J_1 \to J_2$ (by 6.1). % [sic: printed "gives rise to homomorphism", missing "a"]
    72	Conversely, a homomorphism $\psi \colon J_1 \to J_2$ defines a divisorial
    73	correspondence $(1 \times (f^{P_1} \circ \psi))^* \mathcal{M}^{P_2}$ between
    74	$(C_2, P_2)$ and $(C_1, P_1)$.
    75	\hfill $\square$
    76	
    77	In the case that $C$ has a point $P$ rational over $k$, define
    78	$F \colon C \times C \to J$ to be the map
    79	$(P_1, P_2) \mapsto f^P(P_1) - f^P(P_2)$. One checks immediately that this is
    80	independent of the choice of $P$. Thus, if $P \in C(k')$ for some Galois
    81	extension $k'$ of $k$, and $F \colon C_{k'} \times C_{k'} \to J_{k'}$ is the
    82	corresponding map, then $\sigma F = F$ for all
    83	$\sigma \in \Gal(k'/k)$; therefore $F$ is defined over $k$ whether or not $C$
    84	has a $k$-rational point. Note that it is zero on the diagonal $\Delta$ of
    85	$C \times C$.

    11	\paragraph{5. Cohomology and base change.}
    12	At this point, we have to digress to prove a theorem of Grothendieck on the
    13	behavior of cohomology groups of a family of vector bundles $E_y$ on a family
    14	of varieties $X_y$, parametrized by points $y \in Y$ where $X_y$ is assumed
    15	to be a flat family of varieties. An important consequence of this result is
    16	the semicontinuity of the dimensions of the cohomology groups of the $E_y$.
    17	
    18	We assume the following basic result.
    19	
    20	\paragraph{Theorem.}
    21	\textit{If $f : X \to Y$ is a proper morphism of locally noetherian
    22	preschemes and $\mathcal{F}$ a coherent sheaf of $\mathcal{O}_X$-modules on
    23	$X$, for all $p \geq 0$ the direct image sheaves $R^p f_*(\mathcal{F})$ are
    24	coherent sheaves of $\mathcal{O}_Y$-modules.}
    25	
    26	We recall the following definition. If $f : X \to Y$ is a morphism of
    27	preschemes and $\mathcal{F}$ a quasicoherent sheaf on $X$, $\mathcal{F}$ is
    28	said to be \textit{flat over $Y$} or \textit{$f$-flat} if for each
    29	$x \in X$, $\mathcal{F}_x$ (for its natural structure of
    30	$\mathcal{O}_{Y, f(x)}$-module) is $\mathcal{O}_{Y, f(x)}$-flat. It is easily
    31	shown that this condition is equivalent to requiring that for $U \subset X$,
    32	$V \subset Y$ with $U$ and $V$ affine open, and $f(U) \subset V$,
    33	$\mathcal{F}(U)$ is a flat $\mathcal{O}_Y(V)$-module.
    34	
    35	The main result of this section is the following
    36	
    37	\paragraph{Theorem.}
    38	\textit{Let $f : X \to Y$ be a proper morphism of noetherian schemes with
    39	$Y = \Spec A$ affine, and $\mathcal{F}$ a coherent sheaf on $X$, flat over
    40	$Y$. There is a finite complex
    41	$K^{\cdot} : 0 \to K^0 \to K^1 \to \cdots \to K^n \to 0$
    42	of finitely generated projective $A$-modules and an isomorphism of functors}
    43	\[
    44	  H^p(X \times_Y \Spec B, \mathcal{F} \otimes_A B)
    45	    \cong H^p(K^{\cdot} \otimes_A B), \quad (p \geq 0)
    46	\]
    47	\textit{on the category of $A$-algebras $B$.}
    48	
    49	\paragraph{Proof.}
    50	Choose a finite affine covering $\mathfrak{A} = \{U_i\}_{i \in I}$ of $X$ by
    51	affine open subsets. Then the \v{C}ech complex
    52	$C^{\cdot} = C^{\cdot}(\mathfrak{A}, \mathcal{F})
    53	  = \oplus\, C^p(\mathfrak{A}, \mathcal{F})$
    54	of alternating \v{C}ech cochains on $\mathfrak{A}$ with coefficients in
    55	$\mathcal{F}$ is a finite complex of $A$-flat modules, whose cohomologies are
    56	isomorphic to the cohomology groups $H^p(X, \mathcal{F})$.
    57	% [proof continues on the next page]

    25	$H^p(K^{\cdot} \otimes_A B) \to H^p(C^{\cdot} \otimes_A B)$ is an

    27	
    28	\paragraph{Lemma 2.}
    29	\textit{Let $C^{\cdot}$, $K^{\cdot}$ be any finite complexes of flat
    30	$A$-modules, and let $C^{\cdot} \to K^{\cdot}$ be a homomorphism of
    31	complexes inducing isomorphisms
    32	$H^p(C^{\cdot}) \xrightarrow{\ \sim\ } H^p(K^{\cdot})$ for all $p$. Then for
    33	every $A$-algebra $B$, the maps
    34	$H^p(C^{\cdot} \otimes_A B) \xrightarrow{\ \sim\ }

    36	
    37	\paragraph{Proof.}
    38	Construct the `mapping cylinder' $L^{\cdot}$ exactly as in the proof of
    39	Lemma 1. As before, we see that $L^{\cdot}$ is an exact finite complex of
    40	flat $A$-modules. Then it is easy to see that all the modules
    41	$Z^p = \Ker(L^p \xrightarrow{\ \partial^p\ } L^{p+1})$ are flat too, hence
    42	\[
    43	  0 \longrightarrow Z^p \longrightarrow L^p \longrightarrow Z^{p+1}
    44	    \longrightarrow 0
    45	\]
    46	is a short exact sequence of flat $A$-modules. Therefore
    47	\[
    48	  0 \longrightarrow Z^p \otimes_A B \longrightarrow L^p \otimes_A B
    49	    \longrightarrow Z^{p+1} \otimes_A B \longrightarrow 0
    50	\]
    51	is exact, from which it follows that $L^{\cdot} \otimes_A B$ is exact. But
    52	now $L^{\cdot} \otimes_A B$ is the mapping cylinder of the map
    53	$K^{\cdot} \otimes_A B \to C^{\cdot} \otimes_A B$. So using the cohomology
    54	sequence in reverse, it follows that
    55	$H^p(K^{\cdot} \otimes_A B) \to H^p(C^{\cdot} \otimes_A B)$ are
    56	isomorphisms.

490	
   491	Over a separably closed field \(k'\) the construction is Milne \S 4. Fix
   492	\(r \ge 2g+1\) and a degree-\(r\) divisor scheme \(Z\). For a tuple \(\Sigma\) of
   493	\(r-g\) rational points of \(C' = C \times_k k'\), the locus
   494	\[
   495	  C^\Sigma
   496	    = \{\, t \in Z : h^0\bigl(\mathcal{O}(W - \Sigma)_t\bigr) = 1 \,\}
   497	\]
   498	is open, because \(h^0\) is upper semicontinuous and \(h^0 \ge \chi = 1\) in
   499	degree \(g\); adding \(\Sigma\) back to the canonical divisor family of the
   500	rigidified pushforward gives a second map \(C^\Sigma \to Z\), and the equaliser
   501	\(J^\Sigma\) of the two represents the subfunctor of degree-\(r\) classes
   502	\(\mathcal{L}\) with \(h^0(\mathcal{L}(-\Sigma)_t) = 1\) at every point. These
   503	subfunctors cover, so gluing them represents \(\Pic^r_{C'/k'}\). Descent to
   504	\(k\) is a finite Galois quotient, and the degrees assemble as a coproduct over
   505	\(\mathbb{Z}\) through the translation isomorphisms
   506	\(\Pic^d \cong \Pic^r\) given by tensoring with \(\mathcal{O}((r-d) x_0)\).
   507	
   508	The two inputs the route rests on that the quotient route does not are the
   509	rigidified pushforward and the finite Galois quotient. The first is local freeness
   510	of \(q_* \mathcal{L}\) together with its compatibility with base change, and it
   511	holds for every curve satisfying the hypotheses of this chapter
   512	(\cref{thm:rigid_pushforward_gate}). The second is Speiser descent together with
   513	the existence of \(\Gamma\)-stable affine neighbourhoods.
   514	
   515	\begin{theorem}[Local freeness of the rigidified pushforward]\leanok
   516	  \label{thm:rigid_pushforward_locally_free}
   517	  \lean{AlgebraicGeometry.Adelic.rigidPushforwardLocallyFree_proved}
   518	  \uses{lem:p1_integral}
   519	  \source{mumford-abelian-varieties:page-0054}
   520	  \textit{Source: [Mumford], \emph{Abelian Varieties}, II \S 5.}
   521	  Let \(C\) be a smooth proper geometrically integral curve over a field \(k\),
   522	  let \(A\) be a finitely generated \(k\)-algebra and \(q : C_A \to \Spec A\) the
   523	  constant family. Let \(\mathcal{L}\) be an invertible sheaf on \(C_A\) such that
   524	  for every point \(t\) of \(\Spec A\) some two-chart affine cover of the fibre
   525	  \(C_t\) has surjective {\v C}ech difference map on \(\mathcal{L}_t\) --- for a
   526	  separated fibre with affine chart intersection this computes
   527	  \(H^1(C_t, \mathcal{L}_t) = 0\). Then every point of \(\Spec A\) has an open
   528	  neighbourhood on which \(q_* \mathcal{L}\) is free of rank
   529	  \(h^0(C_t, \mathcal{L}_t)\).
   530	\end{theorem}
   531	
   532	\begin{remark}[Why the vanishing hypothesis is stated {\v C}ech-locally]
   533	  \label{rem:fiber_h1_vanishing_form}
   534	  \uses{thm:rigid_pushforward_locally_free}
   535	  The hypothesis of \cref{thm:rigid_pushforward_locally_free} asks for
   536	  \emph{some} two-chart cover of each fibre with surjective difference map,
   537	  rather than for vanishing of the sheaf cohomology \(H^1(C_t, \mathcal{L}_t)\).
   538	  On a separated fibre whose two charts have affine intersection the {\v C}ech
   539	  complex of that cover computes the sheaf cohomology, so the two agree; the
   540	  existential form is the weaker-looking one and is implied by any form of
   541	  \(h^1 = 0\), so a consumer supplying sheaf vanishing supplies this. The
   542	  identification is cover-independent by Mayer--Vietoris, but that
   543	  independence is not itself established here, which is why the hypothesis is
   544	  stated in the form that does not presuppose it.
   545	\end{remark}

    11	% [this Corollary is printed unnumbered; later proofs (pp. 52, 54) refer to it as Corollary 1]
    12	\paragraph{Corollary.}
    13	\textit{Let $X$, $Y$, $f$ and $\mathcal{F}$ be as in the theorem (except
    14	that $Y$ need not be affine). Then we have:}
    15	\begin{itemize}
    16	  \item[(a)] \textit{For each $p \geq 0$, the function $Y \to \mathbf{Z}$
    17	    defined by \\
    18	    $y \longmapsto \dim_{k(y)} H^p(X_y, \mathcal{F}_y)$ is upper
    19	    semicontinuous on $Y$.}
    20	  \item[(b)] \textit{The function $Y \to \mathbf{Z}$ defined by}
    21	    \[
    22	      y \to \chi(\mathcal{F}_y)
    23	        = \sum_{p=0}^{\infty} (-1)^p \dim_{k(y)} H^p(X_y, \mathcal{F}_y)
    24	    \]
    25	    \textit{is locally constant on $Y$.}
    26	\end{itemize}
    27	
    28	\paragraph{Proof.}
    29	The problem being local on $Y$, we may assume $Y$ affine. Let $K^{\cdot}$ be
    30	a complex as in the proposition; by further localization, we may assume
    31	$K^{\cdot}$ to be a free complex. Denote by $d^p : K^p \to K^{p+1}$ the
    32	coboundary of $K$. We then have
    33	\[
    34	\begin{aligned}
    35	  \dim_{k(y)} H^p(X_y, \mathcal{F}_y)
    36	    &= \dim_{k(y)}[\ker(d^p \otimes_A k(y))] - {} \\
    37	    &\qquad\qquad - \dim_{k(y)}[\Image(d^{p-1} \otimes_A k(y))] \\
    38	    &= \dim_{k(y)}[K^p \otimes k(y)]
    39	       - \dim_{k(y)}[\Image(d^p \otimes k(y))] - {} \\
    40	    &\qquad\qquad - \dim_{k(y)}[\Image(d^{p-1} \otimes k(y))].
    41	       \qquad (*)
    42	\end{aligned}
    43	\]
    44	The first term being constant on $Y$, (b) follows on taking alternating sum
    45	of $(*)$ over all $p$. We assert that for any $p \geq 0$, the function

  1377	  commutes with extension of \(k\)

  1393	  solvable, properness will follow once we show that every

  1404	  \(C \times T\) is normal and integral, every invertible sheaf is the

  2925	subscheme.  Furthermore, the connected component of the identity
  2926	$\IPicz_{X/k}$ is an open and closed group subscheme of finite type; it
  2927	is geometrically irreducible; and forming it commutes with extending
  2928	$k$.

  2935	\begin{thm}\label{th:qpp&p}
  2936	 Assume $S$ is the spectrum of a field $k$.  Assume $X/k$ is projective
  2937	and geometrically integral.  Then $\IPicz_{X/k}$ exists and is
  2938	quasi-projective.  If also $X/k$ is geometrically normal, then
  2939	$\IPicz_{X/k}$ is projective.
  2940	 \end{thm}
  2941	 \begin{proof} 
  2942	 Theorem~\ref{th:main} implies $\IPic_{X/k}$ exists and represents
  2943	$\Pic_{(X/k)\et}$, so $\Pic_{(X/k)\fppf}$.  Hence $\IPicz_{X/k}$ exists
  2944	and is of finite type by Proposition~\ref{prp:pic0} (in fact, here
  2945	Proposition~\ref{prp:lft} is logically unnecessary since $\IPic_{X/k}$
  2946	is locally of finite type by Theorem~\ref{th:main}).  So $\IPicz_{X/k}$
  2947	is quasi-projective by Exercise~\ref{ex:q-proj}.
  2948	
  2949	Suppose $X$ is also geometrically normal.  Since $\IPicz_{X/k}$ is
  2950	quasi-projective, to prove it is projective, it suffices to prove it is
  2951	proper.  By Lemma~\ref{lem:agps}, forming $\IPicz_{X/k}$ commutes
  2952	with extending $k$.  And by \cite[2.7.1(vii)]{EGAIV2}, a $k$-scheme is
  2953	complete if (and only if) it is after extending $k$.  So we may, and do,
  2954	assume $k$ is algebraically closed.
  2955	
  2956	Recall the structure theorem of Chevalley and Rosenlicht for algebraic
  2957	groups, or reduced connected group schemes of finite type over $k$; see
  2958	\cite[Thm.~1.1, p.~3]{Co02}.  The theorem says that every algebraic
  2959	group is an extension of an Abelian variety (or complete algebraic
  2960	group) by a linear (or affine) algebraic group.  Recall also that every
  2961	solvable linear algebraic $k$-group is triangularizable (the
  2962	Lie--Kolchin theorem); so, if it's nontrivial, then it contains a copy
  2963	of the multiplicative group or of the additive group; see \cite[(10.5)
  2964	and (10.2)]{Bo69}.  Now,  $\IPic_{X/k}$ is commutative, so solvable.
  2965	Hence it suffices to show that, if $T$ denotes the
  2966	affine line minus the origin, then every $k$-map $t\:T\to
  2967	(\IPicz_{X/k})_{\red}$ is constant.
  2968	
  2969	Since $k$ is algebraically closed, $X/k$ has a section.  So $t$
  2970	arises from an invertible sheaf $\mc L$ on $X\x T$ by the Comparison
  2971	Theorem, Theorem~\ref{th:cmp}.  Since $X\x T$ is integral, there is a
  2972	divisor $D$ such that $\mc O(D)=\mc L$ by \cite[Ex.~II, 6.15,
  2973	p.~145]{Ha83}.
  2974	
  2975	Form the projection $p\:X\x T \to X$.  Restrict $\mc L$ to its generic
  2976	fiber.  This restriction is trivial as $T$ is an open subset of the
  2977	line.  So there is a rational function $\phi$ on $X\x T$ such that
  2978	$(\phi)+D$ restricts to the trivial divisor.  Let $s\:X\to X\x T$ be a
  2979	section.  Set $E:=s^*((\phi)+D)$; then $E$ is a well-defined divisor on
  2980	$X$.  Plainly, $p^*E$ and $(\phi)+D$ coincide as cycles; whence, they
  2981	coincide as divisors by \cite[Prp.~(3.10), p.~139]{AK70}, since $X\x T$
  2982	is normal.  Therefore, $\mc L=p^*\mc O(E)$.  Thus $t\:T\to \IPic_{X/k}$
  2983	is constant.

---
name: horizon-inbox
description: Read and act on the Archon Horizon inbox — list/filter items, understand labels/kinds, comment, archive, create; per-team ownership and read-state; and message other projects or teams via the `horizon inbox` CLI.
---

The inbox is the durable channel between the human, agent sessions (present and
future), and other projects. Act on it through the CLI; never edit inbox files
by hand. Prefer `--json` whenever reading command output for exact ids or
fields.

## Read

- `horizon inbox list` — read the inbox. Use `--json` when you need exact ids,
  labels, scope, author, audience, timestamps, or comments. Use the list filters
  to narrow without losing the overview: `--to horizon`, `--to human`,
  `--project P`, repeated `--kind K`, repeated `--label L`,
  `--status open`, `--query TEXT`, `--limit N`, and `--comments N`.
- In an agent session, an unqualified list means the **open working queue**, not
  archived history. It is ordered by attention: required protections first,
  unread/direct conversations next, then advisory items. JSON starts with an
  `attention` summary so redirecting stderr cannot erase this signal.
- `horizon inbox show <id> --json` opens exactly one item and marks it read for
  your team. Use `--no-mark-read` for inspection without acknowledgement.
- Every inbox command evaluates the full local working set, even when `list` is
  filtered. Treat its advisory warnings as a prompt to review duplicates, stale
  memories, and consumed notices. The CLI never archives automatically because
  only the working agent can decide what is resolved; that agent must make an
  explicit cleanup pass before its final report.
- Labels are the release gate. Local inbox items default to `agent-ready`, which
  means they are visible to agents at run boundaries. Keep that default for
  machine-addressed work, and usually keep it for human-addressed notices too:
  it helps later agents see that the human has already been notified and avoids
  duplicate reports. Use `not-ready`, `rejected`, or no labels only when there is
  a concrete reason agents should not see or act on the item yet.
- Audience says who should read the item: empty/general, `horizon`, `human`,
  `project:<name>`, or a **direct message** to another team: `task:<id>` /
  `run:<id>` (older items may carry the legacy `ground` audience). A conversation
  may have several recipients; start one with `horizon inbox dm <recipient>...`.
  Scope/project says what the item is about.
- Horizon reads general items, items addressed to `horizon`, items addressed
  to its project, and DMs addressed to its own task/run. It should ignore other
  projects' and other teams' addressed items.
- A conversation's participants are its recipients **and its initiator**. The
  initiator is recorded as `metadata.started_by`; replies become unread for every
  other participant, including that initiator. Participants are not ownership:
  the initiator remains responsible for deciding when the thread is finished.
- Kinds: `conversation` (a direct/group thread requiring prompt acknowledgement),
  `hint` (normal guidance), `issue` (problem to fix/report),
  `protection` (standing constraint / soft freeze), `info` (a notice for the
  human — something you did or noticed they should know, e.g. a renamed project
  or an important change; purely informational, never affects what runs),
  `memory` (durable agent note or dead end).

## Ownership & read-state (your team's inbox)

Each running session is a **team**, and the inbox is shared across teams. Two
lightweight overlays keep it navigable:

- **Ownership** — an item is either *shared with everyone* (the default) or
  *owned by one task* (that team's private inbox — e.g. its own memory). Read your
  team's inbox with `horizon inbox list --mine` (owned-by-you **plus** shared);
  another team's private items don't appear. Own an item to your task with
  `horizon inbox add --mine …` (or `--owner <task-id>`), and `horizon inbox own
  <id> --mine|--owner <task>|--shared` to move an existing one. Owning your
  `--kind memory` notes keeps another team's memory out of your working set.
- **Read-state** — read/unread is **per team**, so a shared item several teams see
  tracks who has read it. `horizon inbox list --unread` is what *you* have not read
  yet; `horizon inbox read <id>` marks it read, and `horizon inbox unread <id>`
  puts it back (e.g. you read it but it still needs action). Combine:
  `horizon inbox list --mine --unread` is your team's fresh queue — the same signal
  the pre-command synchronizer counts for you.

Read in this order before editing:

1. `horizon inbox list --mine --status open --kind protection --json` — every
   active protection is required even if your team previously marked it read.
2. `horizon inbox list --mine --unread --kind conversation --json` — open each
   result with `inbox show`; reply when a response is needed, otherwise the read
   acknowledgement clears it until another participant replies.
3. Consult hint/issue/info/memory items as advisory context for the task.

The reader/owner id is inferred from your session (your task), so you rarely pass
it explicitly.

## Act

Authorship is automatic: every item and comment you create through the CLI is
attributed to your role (normally `horizon`) from the run environment — you do
**not** pass `--author` (a stray `--author work-reviewer` is demoted to the
`agent` metadata, not used as the author, so the author set stays conventional).
If you are a dispatched **subagent**, add `--agent <your-name>` (e.g. `--agent
work-reviewer`) to record your identity; it is stored in metadata and shown
next to the role in the UI, keeping the author itself a clean role. Items and
comments are also auto-tagged with the run/session provenance (a small chip in the
UI); you do not pass this yourself.

New inbox items use a two-part body:

- First paragraph = concise title. Keep it short enough to scan in one UI row
  (aim for under ~100 characters); do not put the full explanation here.
- Second paragraph and later = non-empty description. Put the evidence, impact,
  next action, and relevant ids/files here. The description is **mandatory** — an
  item that is only a title is rejected.

Write bodies and comments in **Markdown**: the dashboard renders it. Operational
messages are deltas, not reports. Default to one sentence or at most three short
bullets covering conclusion, new evidence, and next action; do not repeat the
thread, commit diff, or session history. Use headings only when a genuinely
multi-part decision needs them. Agent comments target at most 600 characters and
are rejected above 1200; descriptions/opening messages target 800 and are
rejected above 2400. Humans are not subject to these bounds.

Do not create an item whose body is only a title. If you need a `[persistent]` or
`[temporary]` tag, put it at the start of the title paragraph and keep the rest
of that paragraph concise.

Before opening a new item, search the open inbox for the same topic using
`horizon inbox list --status open --query "key words" --json` and, when relevant,
`--project P` / `--to R`. If a live item already covers the same issue, do not
open a duplicate: add a comment with the new evidence, or edit the body if the
main description is stale. If you discover an open item is obsolete, already
solved, consumed, or superseded, add a short comment when the reason is not
obvious and then run `horizon inbox archive <id>`.

### Conversation lifecycle

A conversation is for an expected reply, decision, or active coordination. A
one-way handoff or announcement is an `info`/`hint`, not a conversation.

1. **Search before starting:** inspect open conversations for the same topic and
   participants (`inbox list --status open --kind conversation --query "key words"
   --json`). Reply to the existing thread whenever it can carry the update. Do not
   open one thread per incremental finding.
2. **One question, one thread:** keep follow-ups, answers, corrections, and the
   final decision as comments on that thread. Start another only when it has a
   genuinely different decision boundary or participant set.
3. **Answer before branching:** when a conversation becomes unread, open it and
   answer or acknowledge it before starting another conversation with the same
   team.
4. **The initiator closes:** if `metadata.started_by` is your task/run, you own
   the lifecycle. Once the requested answer has arrived and been consumed, add a
   short conclusion comment when the outcome is not obvious, then
   `horizon inbox archive <id>`. Do this during the session, not only after a
   warning says the inbox is full.
5. **Do not hide an answer from its initiator:** recipients normally reply and
   leave closure to the initiator. For a human-started thread, answer it but leave
   it open for the human to consume/archive unless the human explicitly delegates
   closure. Use `complete` instead of `archive` only when the concluded thread is
   intentionally meant to remain visible in the resolved working record.
6. **End-of-session sweep:** before the final report, inspect open conversations
   in which your task is `started_by`. Archive every resolved one and state a real
   blocker on any that must remain open. An accumulation of open conversations is
   unfinished coordination, not harmless history.

- `horizon inbox comment <id> --body "..."` — progress note on an item (record
  what changed; not to ask the human for clarification). Do not write your name
  into the body; authorship is automatic. Comment only at a **key advance** such
  as a milestone, ruled-out route, blocker, correction, or conclusion. Update the
  existing thread with the delta instead of re-establishing its full context.
- `horizon inbox dm task:<id> [task:<id> ...] --body "Topic\n\nOpening message"`
  — start a one-to-one or group conversation. Use `horizon ps` to discover live
  teams. Use it only after the lifecycle search above. The sender remains a
  participant and owns closure; every reply makes the thread unread for the other
  participants. Humans read and reply from the live dashboard.
- **Write comments as mathematics, for a human.** State the key step that
  succeeded in human-readable mathematical language (LaTeX for formulas), naming
  the result and the idea — e.g. "Proved $H^i(X,\mathcal{F})=0$ for $i>\dim X$ by
  reducing to the affine case via Čech cohomology." Mention Lean declaration
  names and file paths only as supporting detail; the substance is the maths, not
  a code changelog. This applies to comments on **roadmap items and tasks** too:
  when a key step lands, record it there in the same mathematical, legible style.
- `horizon inbox archive <id>` — soft-delete: keep the item for the record but
  hide it from the dashboard by default. Use for stale, superseded, consumed, or
  no-longer-key context. Keeping the inbox tidy this way is your job (or the
  janitor subagent's) — prune memory/info so they remain small.
  For a conversation you initiated, this is the normal "discussion finished"
  operation after its answer/conclusion has been consumed.
- `horizon inbox complete <id>` — mark an item resolved only when it records work
  you genuinely concluded and want to keep visible outside the archive. Before
  completing, add a short **conclusion comment**: first the mathematical
  conclusion (what was proved/established, in words + LaTeX), then concise
  metadata (runs, approximate LOC, files/declarations involved). A reader should
  grasp the result and how it was concluded without opening the logs.
- `horizon inbox add --body "Short title\n\nDescription with details and next action." [--to R] [--project P] [--persistent|--temporary] [--agent <name> if a subagent]`
  — open a new item.
  - `--to` is the recipient: `horizon`, `human`, `project:<name>`, or a direct
    message to another team `task:<id>` / `run:<id>`.
    Use `--to project:<name>` to message another project (e.g. "I rewrote your
    `foo` declaration more cleanly, you may want it"); use `--to task:<id>` to
    message a specific running team.
  - `--owner <task-id>` / `--mine` keeps the item in one team's inbox instead of
    the shared default.
  - `--project` says what the item is ABOUT (its subject).
  - `--persistent` / `--temporary` just prepend a `[persistent]` / `[temporary]`
    tag to the body.
  - `--pending` labels the item `not-ready` instead of the default `agent-ready`,
    so it stays invisible to agents until a human releases it.
- `horizon inbox add --kind memory --to horizon --body "Short memory title\n\nDurable fact, convention, or dead end."` — record a durable
  note / dead end. Memory lives in the inbox, so it is rendered in the "Memory"
  section and a human can prune it like any other item.
- `horizon inbox protect --body "..." [--project P] [--file F] [--declaration D] [--blueprint-node N]`
  — add a semantic standing constraint the Horizon agent must respect (a soft freeze),
  e.g. "do not change the signature of `Foo.bar`". These render as a
  "Protected" section; honour them, including semantic ones. For a target that
  must be mechanically blocked before dispatch, the user uses the config-backed
  `horizon freeze add <file|declaration|blueprint-node> <target>` command instead.

Reading convention: an item tagged `[persistent]` is a standing rule — respect
it every round and keep it open while relevant. `[temporary]` (or untagged) is
one-shot — archive it once consumed. Items in the "Protected" section are never
modified.

  2648	  \(\psi'(t) = z \in S_{e'}\).  Then
  2649	  \(\varphi(t) = i(\psi'(t)) = \iota_{e'}(z)\) lies in the image of
  2650	  \(\iota_{e'}\), so the point rank of \(\F\) at \(\varphi(t)\) is \(e'\)
  2651	  (\cref{thm:mem_range_rank_stratum}); it is also \(e\), since
  2652	  \(t \in T_e\) (\cref{thm:point_rank_pullback}).  Hence \(e' = e\): the
  2653	  morphism \(\psi'\) maps \(T_e\) into the open summand \(S_e\) of the
  2654	  coproduct, so \(\psi'|_{T_e}\) factors through the coprojection of
  2655	  \(S_e\) as some \(l'_e : T_e \to S_e\), and
  2656	  \(\iota_e \circ l'_e = i \circ \psi'|_{T_e} = \varphi|_{T_e}\).  The
  2657	  uniqueness in \cref{thm:factor_rank_stratum_unique} forces
  2658	  \(l'_e = l_e\); therefore \(\psi'\) and \(\psi\) agree on every piece
  2659	  \(T_e\), and \(\psi' = \psi\).
  2660	\end{proof}
  2661	
  2662	\section{Application: relative curves}
  2663	\label{sec:flatstrat_curve_application}
  2664	
  2665	Let \(C\) be a smooth proper curve over a field \(k\) and \(T\) a noetherian
  2666	\(k\)-scheme.  To apply \cref{thm:flattening_stratification_exists} to
  2667	\(C \times_k T \to T\), it remains to pass from properness to projectivity.
  2668	
  2669	\begin{lemma}
  2670	[Smooth proper curve over \(k\) is projective]
  2671	  \label{lem:smooth_proper_curve_projective}
  2672	  \uses{def:projective_morphism}
  2673	  \textit{Source: classical; cf.\ [Hartshorne], II.6.7 \& II.7.6 (curves).}
  2674	  Let \(C\) be a smooth proper curve over a field \(k\).  Then \(C \to \Spec k\) is
  2675	  projective.  Consequently, for any noetherian \(k\)-scheme \(T\), the relative
  2676	  curve \(C \times_k T \to T\) is projective in the sense of Grothendieck (there
  2677	  exists a relatively very ample line bundle on \(C \times_k T\) over \(T\)).
  2678	\end{lemma}
  2679	
  2680	\begin{proof}
  2681	  Projectivity of a smooth proper curve over a field is classical
  2682	  ([Hartshorne], II.6.7 / II.7.6; alternatively: every divisor of large
  2683	  positive degree on a smooth proper curve \(C\) is very ample, providing the
  2684	  embedding \(C \hookrightarrow \PP^N_k\) for some \(N\)). Pulling the ample line
  2685	  bundle back along \(C \times_k T \to C\) produces a relatively very ample line
  2686	  bundle on \(C \times_k T\) over \(T\).
  2687	\end{proof}
  2688	
  2689	\begin{corollary}
  2690	
  2691	[Flattening stratification for a coherent sheaf on a relative curve]
  2692	  \label{cor:flattening_stratification_curve}
  2693	  \uses{lem:smooth_proper_curve_projective, thm:flattening_stratification_exists}
  2694	  Let \(k\) be a field, \(C\) a smooth proper curve over \(k\), and \(T\) a noetherian
  2695	  \(k\)-scheme.  Let \(\F\) be a coherent sheaf on \(C \times_k T\). Then the
  2696	  flattening-stratification conclusion of
  2697	  \cref{thm:flattening_stratification_exists} applies: there is a finite
  2698	  set \(I\) of Hilbert polynomials and locally-closed subschemes
  2699	  \(T_f \hookrightarrow T\) for \(f \in I\), set-theoretically covering \(T\)
  2700	  disjointly, such that (a) \(\F|_{C \times_k T_f}\) is flat over \(T_f\) for
  2701	  each \(f\), and (b), after setting \(T'':=\coprod_{f\in I}T_f\), any
  2702	  morphism \(\varphi : T' \to T\) such that \(\varphi^* \F\) on
  2703	  \(C \times_k T'\) is \(T'\)-flat factors uniquely through the canonical
  2704	  morphism \(T'' \to T\).
  2705	\end{corollary}

1	\chapter{The Jacobian as an abelian variety}
     2	\label{chap:Jacobian}
     3	
     4	Let \(C\) be a smooth proper geometrically irreducible curve over a field
     5	\(k\), with genus \(g(C)\).  The Jacobian is constructed uniformly as the
     6	identity component \(\Pic^0_{C/k}\) of the Picard scheme.  It is an abelian
     7	variety of dimension \(g(C)\); when \(g(C)=0\), it is \(\Spec k\).
     8	
     9	\section{Albanese objects}
    10	
    11	\begin{definition}[Albanese universal property of a pointed curve]\leanok
    12	  \label{def:IsAlbanese}
    13	  \lean{AlgebraicGeometry.IsAlbanese}
    14	  Let \(P \in C(k)\).  An abelian variety \(J\) together with a pointed
    15	  morphism \(\iota_P \colon C \to J\) is an \emph{Albanese object} for
    16	  \((C,P)\) if every pointed morphism \(f \colon C \to A\) to an abelian
    17	  variety factors uniquely through \(\iota_P\): there is a unique morphism of
    18	  \(k\)-schemes \(g \colon J \to A\) such that
    19	  \[
    20	    P \circ \iota_P = \eta_J,
    21	    \qquad
    22	    f = \iota_P \circ g.
    23	  \]
    24	\end{definition}
    25	
    26	\begin{remark}
    27	  \label{rem:IsAlbanese_typeclasses}
    28	  The phrase ``abelian variety'' includes the group structure, properness,
    29	  smoothness, and geometric irreducibility of both \(J\) and every target
    30	  \(A\).  These are hypotheses of the universal property, rather than extra
    31	  conclusions inside it.
    32	\end{remark}
    33	
    34	\subsection{The universal morphism}
    35	
   545	\begin{proof}
   546	  This is the geometric-irreducibility assertion carried by the chosen
   547	  Jacobian witness.
   548	\end{proof}
   549	
   550	\begin{remark}
   551	  If \(g(C)=0\), then \(\Jac(C)=\Spec k\).  If \(g(C)=1\) and \(C(k)\) is
   552	  nonempty, the choice of a rational point identifies \(C\) with its

THE REPRICING, and it is the finding. ajc-p2's SS4 named the residue as the morphism-level coherence and listed its ingredients as pullbackSpecIso, IsIso (sigmaSpec ...) and galoisSelfTensorEquiv. NONE OF THE THREE IS NEEDED. The coherence is pullback.lift_fst and pullback.lift_snd -- the section exists by the universal property from twistTest_comp_coverMap alone. What the splitting is needed for is something the residue did not name.

AND THE TWO DIRECTIONS ARE NOT SYMMETRIC, which is why this row is advanced and not closed. Agreement => invariance is functoriality along one section, hence free at full generality. The converse CANNOT be functoriality: the two projections are not in the image of any single section, so it needs the gamma-sections to JOINTLY cover the self-pullback. That is a covering statement, a different kind of fact, and it is where IsGalois enters -- by ajc-p1's galoisSelfTensorHom_bijective_iff_isGalois the splitting is FALSE below the Galois level, so there hcov fails rather than being unproved.

hcov NON-VACUITY, by degenerate substitution per I-1413 rather than asserted: at k' = k the group is trivial, coverMap is an iso, the single section is an iso and generates top, which is covering. So the implication is not conditioned on a false statement. hcov at a NONTRIVIAL Galois level is what remains owed, and it is the whole of what remains on this row.

WHAT THIS DOES NOT DO: k'-side representability untouched, G2's scheme-level quotient untouched. It changes WHICH hypothesis a G1 consumer must supply.

CORRECTION I OWE, on my own r6 claim: I told ajc-p2 that "your Galois binder is forced" on the invariance step and they refuted it from binder lists. They were right about the DESCENT and I am now right about the BRIDGE for a reason neither of us gave: sections 3 and 4 of this file both carry NO IsGalois binder, because the Galois hypothesis is not in either implication -- it is in the ANTECEDENT hcov, which is a hypothesis rather than a binder. So "Galois enters exactly once, at the bridge" is correct, and it enters as a covering property, not as an instance.

RESIDUE LOCATED, and attempted rather than only named. hcov_iff_scheme_level: membership in the slice topology IS membership of the transported sieve on the underlying scheme (GrothendieckTopology.mem_over_iff, free). So hcov is not about the slice, the test T, or picEt -- it is that the Gal-indexed family of SCHEME morphisms (coverSelfSection T gamma).left etale-covers the self-pullback. I tried to close it at a nontrivial Galois level and did NOT: infer_instance for IsOpenImmersion (coverSelfSection T gamma).left FAILS there, with the sorryAx control live in the same probe so it is not a stale-import artefact. The covering property is therefore not free from the etale-precoverage machinery, and a lane closing this row must build it. That is what remains, and it is the whole of what remains.

THREE AUDIT FINDINGS AGAINST THIS ROW'S OWN OUTPUT, all reproduced by me and fixed in-tree (commit b85ecf497a). Inherit the corrected forms, not the paragraphs above them.
 * I-1454, the serious one: MY hcov NON-VACUITY WITNESS SITS WHERE THE CONSEQUENT IS FREE. At Mono (specMapAlgebra k k') cancel_mono forces EVERY gamma to the identity, so the twist is the identity, hinv is free, and the two projections COINCIDE -- projections_agree_of_invariant's conclusion holds there with NEITHER hypothesis. Landed as theorems specGal_eq_id_of_mono and twistTest_eq_id_of_mono. So hcov is SATISFIABLE and no exhibited model separates the two projections.  * I-1458 (ajc-p2): "closing this row means building it" OVER-PRICES hcov. The topology half is ONE LINE (zariskiTopology_le_etaleTopology of a Cover). Only the open-immersion half is owed, and even there a failed inferInstance is not absence: IsOpenImmersion (Sigma.iota ...) is a THEOREM whose instance search also fails, at the very object selfTensorSpecCoproduct produces.

SO THE RESIDUE, corrected twice and now stated once: the MIDDLE step only -- base change of selfTensorSpecCoproduct along T_k' -> Spec k', then matching the coproduct's gamma-component to coverSelfSection T gamma.
